description: §6.5.1 a reactive mutating method called with SEVERAL arguments, one of which reads a cell, receives each argument separately. #ins runs `@ls.splice(0, 0, @ins9)`, which inserts 9 at the front: [9,1,2]. #add runs `@ls.push(@ins9, @k)`, which appends 9 and 1: [9,1,2,9,1]. #wipe runs `@ls.fill(@v, 0, 2)`, which zeroes indexes 0-1: [0,0,2,9,1]. The case pins s461 (gap g-splice-multi-arg-comma-expression-s459): the argument list was lowered as ONE comma expression (`splice((0, 0, ins9))`), which passed only the last value, so the insert was silently lost.
rationale: §6.5.1 lists `@arr.splice(start, deleteCount, ...items)` among the mutating methods valid on reactive arrays, and the call performs that method's ordinary JavaScript mutation. Each argument is a separate argument. Nothing in §6.5 makes them one expression. So splice(0, 0, 9) inserts 9 at index 0, push(9, 1) appends both values, and fill(0, 0, 2) zeroes indexes 0 and 1. After #ins, #add and #wipe, @ls is [0,0,2,9,1] and #out shows it.
